clue.text: Note fellow, mostly silent, is holding back capital

indicators.note: the fellow-plus-silent string holds the next piece inside it, keeping it captive

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: back says the capital city's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

indicators.note: 'mostly' cuts a letter off

parts.note: DUMB is what 'silent' stands for

explanation.surface: A note about a quiet man who withholds funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the capital, and 'is holding' puts it inside the fellow-plus-silent string, splitting the fellow after its first letter. 'capital' looks like money but is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorandum is a written note or reminder, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Material cut up and given close inspection

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole string is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: denim is a cotton material
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: Cloth is cut and checked carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DENIM + AXE as one run. 'cut up' looks like chopped, but 'cut' is AXE and 'up' the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Examined means inspected closely, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Released from prison, uncouth type's heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: a lout is an uncouth type; the 's is a link meaning is. That the letters also sit inside the word uncouth is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A freed thug sets off.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner who is out has been released.

clue.text: Man at bottom of a gangway

indicators.note: in a down clue at bottom of puts the island beneath the A

parts.note: the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man stands at the foot of a gangway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the island, the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between seats, a gangway.

clue.text: System of rule by chapter covered in book

indicators.note: covered in says the chapter is enclosed by the book

parts.note: a diary is a book

explanation.surface: Governance by a cathedral chapter recorded in a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Diarchy is a system of government by two rulers jointly.

clue.text: Cereal running short? Not in a thousand years

indicators.note: running short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: millet is a cereal grain
nary is a dialect word meaning not any

explanation.surface: Cereal will not run out in a millennium.
explanation.definitionFit: A millenary is a period of a thousand years.

clue.text: This is used in post-natal care

definitions.text: This is used in post-natal care

indicators.note: used in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across the hyphen and space

explanation.surface: A remark on baby powder in caring for a newborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum powder is the classic thing dusted on a baby after bathing, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Performance so far consisting of one song on disc?

definitions.meaning: the history of someone's achievements to date

definitions.text: consisting of one song on disc?
definitions.meaning: a single number on a record, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: A track record is past performance; whimsically, a record holding a single track.

clue.text: Improve appearance, with classy lick of paint

parts.note: a look is an appearance
U means upper-class

indicators.note: a lick of paint is a small amount, here its first letter

explanation.surface: Smarten up your look with some posh paintwork.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Things looking up are improving; the phrasal verb means get better.

clue.text: Film buff attending Man From Van Diemen's Land

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, a fan

indicators.note: From here means taken away from, so the man is removed from the island's name

parts.note: Van Diemen's Land is the old name for Tasmania
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film enthusiast goes to see a film about a Tasmanian.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics suggest a film title; in fact 'Man From' tells you to take MAN out of TASMANIA, leaving TASIA. 'attending' just joins FAN to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the 1940 Disney animated film set to classical music.

clue.text: Pressurise the French shortly

parts.note: le is French for the
anon is an old word for soon, shortly

explanation.surface: Squeeze the French a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean on someone is an idiom for putting pressure on them.

clue.text: In conclusion, to use trickery's no good

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter for good is taken away

parts.note: to finagle is to obtain by trickery

explanation.surface: Finally, cheating is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as part of the definition but is a link; FINAGLE loses its G to leave the last part of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a performance, its conclusion.

clue.text: Actually how live broadcast is transmitted?

definitions.meaning: in fact, as it turns out
a live show goes out in real time, while events occur

explanation.definitionFit: As it happens means in fact, and live coverage is sent out while events occur.

clue.text: Ask about the time one must leave hotel?

definitions.meaning: to make enquiries about something, to investigate it

definitions.text: the time one must leave hotel?
definitions.meaning: the hour by which a guest has to vacate the room

explanation.definitionFit: Check out means investigate as a verb, and as a noun it is the time hotel guests must depart.

clue.text: Cavalier survived about a month, before getting caught by a military unit

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for survived is read backwards

parts.note: survived means lived
May is a month
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A Cavalier soldier lived through a month before capture by a regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LIVED into DEVIL. 'Cavalier' looks like a Civil War royalist; it is the adjective meaning carefree.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavalier as an adjective means offhand and reckless, the same as carefree and heedless.

clue.text: Sensational play made moral in translation

indicators.note: in translation suggests the words are turned into another form, the letters reordered

explanation.surface: A lurid play made moral when translated.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a play with exaggerated, sensational events and characters.

clue.text: Notable European place is in need of restoration

indicators.note: in need of restoration says the letters are damaged and must be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A notable European site needs restoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of restoration' rearranges PLACE IS to SPECIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial means special or notable, a dated synonym.

clue.text: Compromise for the rest of the travellers?

definitions.meaning: a position midway between two extremes

definitions.text: for the rest of the travellers?
definitions.meaning: an inn placed midway along a route where travellers stop to rest

explanation.definitionFit: A halfway house is figuratively a compromise and literally an inn midway on a journey.

clue.text: Remove tiny feeling of uncertainty, so to speak

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny

indicators.note: so to speak says the word for uncertainty is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: doubt is a feeling of uncertainty

explanation.surface: Get rid of a small nagging doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: To weed out is to remove unwanted elements, as from a garden.

clue.text: Certainly not what one cured of phobia has

definitions.text: what one cured of phobia has
definitions.meaning: someone freed of a phobia lacks dread

explanation.definitionFit: No fear is British slang for certainly not, and literally the state of having no dread.

clue.text: Friend concerned with backing old politician taken in by bounder

indicators.note: backing says the piece for concerned with comes at the back, after the rest
taken in by says the old politician goes inside the bounder

parts.note: a bounder is a cad, an ungentlemanly man
MP is a Member of Parliament
re means about, concerned with

explanation.surface: A friend supports an old MP conned by a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but places RE at the end of C(OMP)AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Compadre is a Spanish-derived word for a close friend or companion.

clue.text: One offers beer — abstainer goes for doctor

indicators.note: goes for says one piece gives way to another, the doctor replacing the teetotaller

parts.note: bitter is a British type of beer
TT means teetotal, an abstainer from alcohol
DD is Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: Someone offers a drink, but the teetotaller fetches a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidder is one who makes an offer, as at an auction.

clue.text: Gosh! Sweet manufacturer's slogan when advertising on air

indicators.note: on air says the slogan is broadcast, so heard spoken

parts.note: a sweet maker's advert might urge purchase of chewing gum

explanation.surface: A confectioner's radio jingle provokes surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: BY GUM is a northern English exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: By gum is a mild northern English oath, an exclamation like gosh.

clue.text: City providing sanctuary for Cockney, say? Quite the reverse.

indicators.note: Quite the reverse tells you to read the whole assembled string backwards

parts.note: a haven is a sanctuary, and a Cockney drops the H
eg means for example, say

explanation.surface: A city offering refuge to a Londoner, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney (a working-class East Londoner) drops initial H, so haven loses its first letter. 'Quite the reverse' then turns the whole run, giving the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is a major Swiss city on Lake Geneva, so the plain definition names it by category.

clue.text: Performing in drag, wearing extremely offensive dress material

indicators.note: wearing says the outer letters are worn round the scrambled letters, like a garment
extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of offensive
Performing suggests the letters act out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A drag act wearing a deeply offensive frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing' rearranges the two fodder words, and 'wearing' puts the first and last letters of offensive round the result. 'drag' suggests cross-dressing but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine stiff cotton fabric used for dresses.

clue.text: What's the point in writing new book without one?

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the new book goes round one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Asking why bother writing a new book without a single idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A nib is the pointed writing tip of a pen.

clue.text: Experts' ordinary language not English

definitions.note: read with the apostrophe as plural experts, the 's being a link

indicators.note: not says the letter for English is left out

parts.note: prose is ordinary language as opposed to verse

explanation.surface: Specialists use plain words, not English.
explanation.definitionFit: Pros are professionals, people expert at what they do.

clue.text: Transport gold to US town

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
taken as written
Mobile is a city in Alabama

explanation.surface: Ship the gold to an American town.
explanation.definitionFit: An automobile is a car, a means of transport.
